text: What tormented Ivan Ilyich most. <break time="0.8s" /> Was the lie. <break time="0.8s" /> Accepted by everyone around him. <break time="0.8s" /> That he was only ill and not dying. <break time="0.8s" /> And that he needed nothing more. <break time="0.8s" /> Than rest and medicine to recover. <break time="0.8s" /> Only Gerasim. <break time="0.8s" /> A fresh faced young peasant. <break time="0.8s" /> Who had come to serve in the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Did not lie. <break time="0.8s" /> And he performed even the most unpleasant tasks. <break time="0.8s" /> For his master lightly. <break time="0.8s" /> And without any sign of disgust. <break time="0.8s" /> When Ivan Ilyich found. <break time="0.8s" /> That his pain eased. <break time="0.8s" /> If his legs were raised. <break time="0.8s" /> Gerasim sat for hours. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding them on his shoulders. <break time="0.8s" /> And in that position. <break time="0.8s" /> The sick man found a comfort. <break time="0.8s" /> That no doctor had given him. <break time="0.8s" /> When his master apologized for the trouble. <break time="0.8s" /> Gerasim answered with a calm smile. <break time="0.8s" /> We will all die someday. <break time="0.8s" /> So why should I not take a little trouble for you. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan Ilyich understood. <break time="0.8s" /> That Gerasim alone pitied him. <break time="0.8s" /> And he longed. <break time="0.8s" /> Though he was ashamed to admit it. <break time="0.8s" /> To be petted and comforted. <break time="0.8s" /> Like a sick child. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was exactly what no one else would do. <break time="0.8s" /> One evening his wife and daughter. <break time="0.8s" /> Dressed in their finest clothes. <break time="0.8s" /> Came in to see him. <break time="0.8s" /> Before going to the theater. <break time="0.8s" /> Where a famous French actress was performing. <break time="0.8s" /> And their healthy, perfumed presence. <break time="0.8s" /> Felt like an insult. <break time="0.8s" /> Later, alone in the dark. <break time="0.8s" /> He wept like a child. <break time="0.8s" /> Over his helplessness, his loneliness. <break time="0.8s" /> And the cruelty of people and of God. <break time="0.8s" /> Demanding to know. <break time="0.8s" /> Why he had been made to suffer so much. <break time="0.8s" /> Then, as he grew quiet. <break time="0.8s" /> He seemed to hear. <break time="0.8s" /> The voice of his own soul. <break time="0.8s" /> Asking what he really wanted. <break time="0.8s" /> And he answered. <break time="0.8s" /> That he wanted to live. <break time="0.8s" /> To live well and pleasantly. <break time="0.8s" /> As he had before.
